bottomLine: You have €4.3M in traced public funding, well behind German Bionic Systems (€15.0M via EIB) and FFT Produktionssysteme (€7.0M across state aid and Horizon) in your sub-sector.
Your 250+ headcount closes SME-only lanes like EIC Accelerator, but nothing in the screen rules you out of Horizon Europe's consortium-based clusters or Innovation Fund SSP.
Innovation Fund SSP is the fund sized to your €15M-50M ticket: it funds large-scale industrial capex and nothing in its screen closes it to you.
The Horizon EU clusters (CL1, CL3, CL4, Miss) and ERC POC all require a multi-partner consortium, so treat them as routes to pursue only once you have confirmed you can assemble one.
A successful Innovation Fund SSP grant would fund tens of millions of euros of capex directly, without diluting equity or creating repayment obligations.

report.positioning: Frame Neura Robotics against the Clean Industrial Deal's push to widen state aid for industrial manufacturing and against the €234bn European Competitiveness Fund now being negotiated for the 2028 budget, which folds Horizon Europe into four windows including a €125.2bn window for resilience, security, defence, industry and space. Your cognitive humanoid and cobot systems for industrial automation sit inside exactly that window's remit: European industrial capacity building rather than pre-commercial research. At your scale, with a co-financing capacity above 50% of project cost, position the story as industrial deployment and capex readiness, not early-stage R&D. This matters most for Innovation Fund SSP, whose large-scale industrial grants reward demonstrated capacity to co-finance and deploy at scale, and for any Horizon consortium bid, where evaluators weight alignment to the call's stated industrial outcomes. Do not frame this as a deep-tech research story: your headcount and stage put you past that lane, and the political argument favours a scaling industrial producer over an early-stage innovator.
report.stateOfPlay: The clearest movement sits on your own table. The European Commission's proposed European Competitiveness Fund, worth €234bn and folding in Horizon Europe's €175bn from 2028, would consolidate the clusters behind four of your rows (CL1, CL3, CL4, Miss) into four new windows, with a €125.2bn window for resilience, security, defence, industry and space likely closest to your work. This is still being negotiated with the Council and Parliament, so the eligibility rules and window allocations that would govern a future application are not yet fixed. An argument built today on the current cluster's expected outcomes may need reframing once the window structure and its priorities are settled, likely before the fund launches in 2028. Track this design phase now so your positioning is ready when the calls under the new structure open, rather than rebuilding your case after the fact.
report.caveats: Figures shown are committed amounts from public registers on each instrument's own reporting basis, coverage varies by country and instrument, and absence from the database is not proof that no funding was received.
